name: Brightside Health vs Cerebral
title: Brightside Health vs Cerebral: Online Psychiatry Platforms Compared
description: Compare Brightside Health ($95/mo psychiatry, PrecisionRx, measurement-based care) vs Cerebral ($60/mo, no controlled substances). Two leading telehealth psychiatry platforms.

summary.bottom_line: Brightside Health and Cerebral are both online psychiatry platforms, but with key differences. Brightside focuses on measurement-based care with PrecisionRx pharmacogenomic testing ($95/mo psychiatry) and accepts Medicare/Medicaid. Cerebral is cheaper ($60/mo) but no longer prescribes controlled substances after a 2022 DOJ investigation. Choose based on whether you need controlled substances and value clinical outcome tracking.

key_differences.clinical_approach: Brightside: Measurement-based, PrecisionRx | Cerebral: Standard telepsychiatry
key_differences.therapy_add_on: Brightside: $299/mo | Cerebral: Included in higher tiers

sections.heading: Different Clinical Philosophies
sections.content: Brightside Health emphasizes measurement-based care - using validated clinical assessments (PHQ-9, GAD-7) to track outcomes weekly and adjust treatment. Their PrecisionRx pharmacogenomic testing helps identify which medications may work best based on your genetics. Cerebral offers more straightforward telepsychiatry at a lower price point, but their 2022 DOJ investigation led them to stop prescribing controlled substances entirely.

sections.heading: Cost Comparison
sections.content: Cerebral is cheaper: $60/mo vs Brightside's $95/mo for medication management. However, Brightside includes PrecisionRx genetic testing (typically $200+ standalone) and accepts Medicare/Medicaid, which Cerebral doesn't. For therapy, Brightside charges $299/mo separately while Cerebral bundles it at $325/mo total. Insurance can significantly reduce costs on both platforms.

sections.heading: The Controlled Substance Factor
sections.content: The biggest practical difference: Brightside can prescribe controlled substances (stimulants for ADHD, benzodiazepines for severe anxiety) when clinically appropriate. Cerebral stopped all controlled substance prescribing in 2022 after a DOJ investigation into their prescribing practices. If you need ADHD medication or have severe anxiety requiring benzodiazepines, Brightside is your only option between these two.

recommendations.when: You need controlled substances (ADHD stimulants, benzodiazepines) or value measurement-based care with outcome tracking.
You only need non-controlled medications (antidepressants, non-benzo anxiety meds) and want the lowest price.
You have Medicare or Medicaid - Cerebral doesn't accept government insurance.
You want pharmacogenomic testing to help identify the best medication for your genetics.

faqs.q: Can Cerebral prescribe Adderall or other stimulants?
faqs.a: No. Cerebral stopped prescribing all controlled substances (including ADHD stimulants and benzodiazepines) in 2022 following a DOJ investigation. If you need ADHD medication, consider Brightside Health or Done.

PrecisionRx is pharmacogenomic testing that analyzes your DNA to help predict which psychiatric medications may work best for you and which to avoid. It's included in Brightside's psychiatry subscription at no extra cost.
Both accept major commercial insurance. Brightside also accepts Medicare and Medicaid. Check each platform for specific plan coverage in your state.

faqs.q: What happened with Cerebral's DOJ investigation?
faqs.a: In 2022, Cerebral faced DOJ scrutiny over controlled substance prescribing practices. They proactively stopped prescribing all controlled substances. The investigation highlighted concerns about telehealth ADHD treatment oversight.
